query_text: What is biologically happening to your voice when you whisper?

messages.content: What is biologically happening to your voice when you whisper?

message.content:
When you **whisper**, your vocal folds still come together, but they usually don’t vibrate in the same clean, periodic way they do during normal speech. Instead, air passes through a **narrowed, partly closed larynx** and creates **turbulent airflow** plus friction, which is why whispering sounds quieter and more breathy than voiced speech.[4][5]

Biologically, normal voice production works by the vocal folds closing and then vibrating as air from the lungs pushes through them.[4] In whispering, that regular vibration is reduced or absent, and the folds are held in a configuration that can require extra muscular effort; some voice specialists note that many people also unconsciously **strain** while whispering, which can increase tension in the larynx.[1][5]

A practical consequence is that whispering is not always the same as “resting” your voice. Some clinicians report that common whispering styles can be **as irritating as shouting**, because they may increase laryngeal squeeze and friction instead of allowing the vocal folds to stay relaxed.[1][5]

If you want, I can also explain the difference between **normal whispering**, **breathy whispering**, and **the “open-throat whisper”** used in voice training.
